Both declared predecessors are accepted at the recorded snapshot. The finite nonempty compact convex sampled fibers and y in the sampled set meet the hypotheses of 1ec728c26c11b368. The resulting cap is nonvertical, passes through y and has mass D(y), even when y and both endpoints share a base.

The compact body gives a finite sampled base set. Its convexity gives the required compatibility for the positive-depth characterization. That fact applies to both endpoints even when their bases coincide.

For any attaining nonvertical through-y cap, the margins of the endpoints have weighted average zero with strictly positive weights. If m=L(y_e)>0, a ball around y_e in its own fiber contains points with L between 0 and m, because the continuous normal is nonzero. An open smaller portion of the ball in this slab gives strictly positive removed d-volume. The translated closed cap still contains y_e and has mass strictly below D(y)≤D(y_e), a contradiction.

The two margins are therefore zero. A cap of mass D(y) containing each endpoint gives D(y_e)≤D(y), and the reverse bounds are exactly the assumed interpolation equality. Both steps work with equal bases.
